edition.locus: Adversus Marcionem 3.7 (duo aduentus / humilitas et gloria)

source_text: Discat nunc haereticus ei abundanti cum ipso licebit Iudaeo rationem quoque errorum eius, a quo ducatum mutuatus in hac argumentatione, caecus a caeco, in eandem decidit foueam. duos dicimus Christi habitus a prophetis demonstratos totidem aduentus eius praenotasse: unum in humilitate, utique primum, cum tamquam ouis ad uictimam deduci habebat et tamquam agnus ante tondentem sine uoce, ita non aperiens os. ne aspectu quidem honestus. adnuntiauimus enim, inquit. de illo: sicut puerulus, sicut radix in terra sitienti. et non est species eius neque gloria, et uidimus eum. et non habebat speciem neque decorem, sed species eius inhonorata, deficiens citra filios hominum, homo in plaga et sciens ferre infirmitatem, ut positus a patre in lapidem offensionis et petram scandali, minoratus ab eo modicum citra angelos, uermem se pronuntians et non hominem, ignominiam hominis et nullificamen populi. quae ignobilitatis argumenta primo aduentui competunt sicut sublimitatis secundo, cum fiet iam non lapis offensionis nec petra scandali, sed lapis summus angularis post reprobationem adsumptus et sublimatus in consummationem templi, ecclesiae scilicet, et petra sane illa apud Danihelem de monte praecisa, quae imaginem saecularium regnorum comminuet et conteret. de quo aduentu idem prophetes: et ecce cum nubibus caeli tamquam filius hominis ueniens uenit usque ad ueterem dierum. aderat in conspectu eius, et qui adsistebant adduxerunt illum. et data est ei potestas regia et omnes nationes terrae secundum genera et omnis gloria famulabunda. et potestas eius usque in aeuum quae non auferetur, et regnum eius quod non uitiabitur. tunc scilicet habiturus est speciem honorabilem et decorem indeficientem super filios hominum, - tempestiuus enim, inquit, decore citra filios hominum, effusa est gratia in labiis tuis; propterea benedixit te deus in aeuum. accingere ensem super femur tuum, potens tempestiuitate tua et pulchritudine tua — cum et pater, posteaquam diminuit eum modicum quid citra angelos, gloria et honore coronabit illum et subiciet omnia pedibus eius. tunc et cognoscent eum qui compugerunt et caedent pectora sua tribus ad tribum, utique quod retro non agnouerunt eum in humilitate condicionis humanae: et homo est, inquit Hieremias, et quis cognoscet illum? quia et: natiuitatem eius, Esaias, quis, inquit, enarrabit? sic et apud Zachariam in persona Iesu, immo et in ipso nominis sacramento, uerus summus sacerdos patris, Christus Iesus, duplici habitu in duos aduentus deliniatur, primo sordidis indutus, id est carnis passibilis et mortalis indignitate, cum et diabolus aduersabatur ei. auctor scilicet Iudae traditoris, ne dicam etiam post baptisma temptator, dehinc despoliatus pristinas sordes et exornatus podere et mitra et cidari munda, id est secundi aduentus gloria et honore. si enim et duorum hircorum, qui ieiunio offerebantur, faciam interpretationem, nonne et illi utrumque ordinem Christi figurant? pares quidem atque consimiles propter eundem domini conspectum, quia non in alia uenturus est forma, ut qui agnosci habeat a quibus laesus est. alter autem eorum circumdatus coccino, maledictus et consputatus et conuulsus et compunctus, a populo extra ciuitatem abiciebatur in perditionem, manifestis notatus insignibus dominicae passionis, alter uero pro delictis oblatus et sacerdotibus templi in pabulum datus secundae repraesentationis argumenta signabat, qua delictis omnibus expiatis sacerdotes templi spiritalis, id est ecclesiae, dominicae gratiae quasi uisceratione quadam frueren tur, ieiunantibus ceteris a salute. igitur quoniam primus aduentus et plurimum figuris obscuratus et omni inhonestate prostratus canebatur, secundus uero et manifestus et deo condignus. idcirco, quem facile et intellegere et credere potuerunt, eum solum intuentes, id est secundum, non inmerito decepti sunt: circa obscuriorem, certe indigniorem, id est primum. atque ita in hodiernum negant uenisse Christum suum, quia non in sublimitate uenerit, dum ignorant etiam in humilitate fuisse uenturum.
pass_a_gloss: Prophets mark two advents: first humble passion (sheep/lamb, no beauty, stone of offense); second glory (cornerstone, Daniel’s stone, clouds). Missing the humble coming, they deny Christ has come.
pass_b_english: Let the heretic learn — and the Jew too, with whom he may abound — the reason also of that one’s errors, from whom he borrowed lead in this argument, blind from blind, and fell into the same pit. We say two habits of Christ shown by the prophets marked as many advents of his: one in humility, of course the first, when he had to be led like a sheep to the victim and like a lamb before the shearer without voice, so not opening the mouth — not even honest in look. For we announced, he says, about him: like a little child, like a root in thirsty ground. And there is no appearance of him nor glory, and we saw him. And he had no appearance nor beauty, but his appearance was dishonored, failing short of the sons of men — a man in blow and knowing how to bear weakness — set by the Father as a stone of offense and rock of scandal, lessened by him a little under the angels, pronouncing himself a worm and not a man, mankind’s shame and the people’s nullifying. These proofs of lowliness fit the first advent as those of height fit the second, when he will already be not a stone of offense nor rock of scandal, but the chief corner stone taken up after rejection and raised to the temple’s completion — the church, of course — and that rock in Daniel cut from the mountain, which will smash and crush the image of the world’s kingdoms. Of which advent the same prophet: And behold, coming with the clouds of heaven like a son of man he came to the ancient of days. He was present in his sight, and those standing by brought him. And royal power was given him and all nations of the earth by kinds and all glory in service. And his power forever which will not be taken away, and his kingdom which will not be spoiled. Then of course he will have an honorable appearance and beauty that does not fail above the sons of men — for timely, he says, in beauty beyond the sons of men, grace is poured on your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever. Gird the sword on your thigh, powerful in your timing and beauty — when the Father also, after he lessened him a little under the angels, will crown him with glory and honor and put all under his feet. Then also those who pierced him will recognize him and beat their breasts tribe by tribe — of course because earlier they did not recognize him in the humility of the human condition: And he is a man, says Jeremiah, and who will know him? Because also: His nativity, Isaiah, who, he says, will tell? So also in Zechariah in Jesus’ person — indeed in the sacrament of the name itself — the Father’s true high priest, Christ Jesus, is outlined in a double habit into two advents: first clothed in filth, that is the unworthiness of passible and mortal flesh, when the devil also opposed him — author of course of Judas the traitor, not to say also tempter after baptism — then stripped of former filths and adorned with robe and mitre and clean turban, that is the glory and honor of the second advent. For if I also interpret the two goats offered on the fast, do not they too figure either order of Christ? Alike and similar for the same look of the Lord, because he will not come in another form, so that he may be recognized by those who hurt him. But one of them, wrapped in scarlet, cursed and spat on and torn and pierced, was cast by the people outside the city into ruin, marked with clear badges of the Lord’s passion; the other, offered for sins and given as food to the temple priests, signed the proofs of the second showing, by which, all sins expiated, the priests of the spiritual temple — that is the church — would enjoy the Lord’s grace as by a kind of feast, while the rest fast from salvation. Therefore since the first advent was sung both much veiled by figures and laid low by every dishonor, but the second both clear and worthy of God, they were not wrongly deceived who, looking only at the one easy to understand and believe — that is the second — missed the more obscure, certainly more unworthy — that is the first. And so to this day they deny their Christ has come, because he did not come in height, while they do not know he was also going to come in humility.

lemmas.sense: two habits of Christ… as many advents
like a sheep to the victim
stone of offense and rock of scandal
was also going to come in humility

choices.why: aduentus here is coming-times, not Chalcedonian natures.
habitus is prophetic bearing/condition across advents.
in humilitate…uenturum is the denied first coming.

notes: Prophecy/two-comings locus; Creator’s Christ in humility then glory.
